key_insight: GeSn crystalline quality and annealing temperature govern Ni–Ge–Sn intermixing and magnetic behavior, with higher Sn content associated with greater structural degradation.
engineering_relevance: Ni/GeSn integration requires careful thermal-budget control to preserve crystalline quality and limit interfacial alloying that weakens Ni ferromagnetism.
method: Studied 15 nm Ni on GeSn heterostructures with 8% and 10% Sn, annealed at 573 and 973 K for 10 s.
Probed crystal structure and intermixing using X-ray diffraction, pole figures, and XPS depth profiling.
evidence_signal: At 573 K, 8% Sn GeSn retained its texture while 10% Sn developed microtwins; at 973 K, both structures degraded and showed strongly suppressed ferromagnetic response.
watch_item: The 973 K treatment is a severe upper-bound reference, and two compositions and annealing temperatures do not establish a complete processing window.
paper_title: Investigation of the Microstructural and Magnetic Properties of Ni on GeSn Layers
